summary: Sakkyryr Airport (SUK/UEBS) is a small regional airport serving the remote settlement of Batagay-Alyta in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russian Federation. Located in the subarctic tundra of northeastern Siberia, it functions as a vital transport link for one of the coldest inhabited regions on Earth. The facility primarily supports local passenger traffic and serves the surrounding Even and Sakha communities.
faqs:
Q: What is Sakkyryr Airport used for?
A: It serves as a regional gateway for Batagay-Alyta and surrounding villages, primarily handling passenger flights connecting the remote community to larger hubs in Yakutia.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Sakkyryr?
A: Summer months (June through August) offer the most reliable weather and longer daylight hours, while winter operations can be affected by extreme cold temperatures reaching below -50°C.

Q: Are there regular scheduled flights to Sakkyryr?
A: Service is limited and typically operated by small regional carriers using aircraft suited for short unpaved or semi-prepared runways common in Arctic Russia.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Being a small remote airport, facilities are minimal, generally limited to a basic terminal building, with no extensive commercial services on site.
transport_tips: There are no public buses or rail service to Batagay-Alyta, so onward ground transport must typically be pre-arranged through local contacts or the hosting organization. The airport is located near the settlement, meaning short taxi or private vehicle rides are usually the only options. Travelers should confirm transport arrangements before arrival, as ride-hailing apps do not operate in this region.
local_tip: Pack extreme cold-weather gear in winter—layered down clothing, insulated boots, and face protection are essential, as even short walks between the aircraft and terminal can expose you to dangerously low wind-chill temperatures.
